package: Phase 3a: FuzzyDiff, the ninth validated TOPP workflow
scope: The FuzzyDiff TOPP tool and its executable. The comparator it drives is the library port of FuzzyStringComparator (tests/data/fuzzy_string_comparator_provenance.json); the lifecycle is TOPPBase's (tests/data/topp_cli_lifecycle_provenance.json). Sources come from the OpenMS4-topp, OpenMS4-cli and OpenMS4-test-data packages, which are versioned independently of the Core SDK and are deliberately not resolved against it.

upstream_test_definition.note: No FuzzyDiff registration retains an output file: WILL_FAIL is the registered expectation. The executed Release run supplies the exit code and both streams. The comments at 142-143 have the reasons of _1 and _2 swapped.

method: Each oracle case runs through openms::cli::run_with::<FuzzyDiff> in process (two through the built executable, with a working directory), and is compared with the Release build on the exit code, stdout byte for byte and stderr byte for byte. The C++ streams are normalised by the oracle (data directory, case directory, timing values, sort temporary names) and then by the test for the framework's documented differences only: the TOPPBase timing line is dropped (and held to exactly the runs whose main_ returned), the Linux stty probe line of the usage text is dropped, the framework's missing-file parenthetical reads 'does not exist', the strict-update diagnostic and its 'Parameters passed ... are invalid' line are put in code order, and a -sort temporary file is named by its input. -write_ini is compared as a file, line by line and as a decoded parameter tree.
evidence_tier: tier 1 (executed differential): the pinned C++ Release build openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 on ibminode06, 80 FuzzyDiff invocations run twice (../oracle/fuzzy-diff-tool), including the four upstream registrations TOPP_FuzzyDiff_1..4 on their pinned inputs; 77 match in full, 3 are deliberate divergences asserted on their own; tier 4 for the native refusals and the test-support emulation's agreement

oracle.reproducibility: two runs, identical exit codes and streams after normalisation (differ.txt empty)

known_divergences.cpp: exit 10: libstdc++ std::from_chars reports a number that rounds to zero (1e-400) as out of range, so it reads as letters
known_divergences.rust: exit 0: the comparator accepts underflow, as the source comment FuzzyStringComparator.cpp:205-208 states and the libc++ build does; unchanged by the promotion
known_divergences.scope: only values that round to zero; a subnormal, the smallest normal and an overflow agree (token_subnormal, token_min_normal, token_overflow)

known_divergences.cpp: exit 10: with -sort the source's std::getline swallows the read error and compares an empty text
known_divergences.rust: exit 12: the port does not compare a text it could not read, the code the source gives the same directory without -sort

native_boundaries: An input beyond the comparator's MAX_INPUT_BYTES (1 GiB) exits 11 (INCOMPATIBLE_INPUT_DATA), with and without -sort, and so does a -sort input beyond FuzzyDiff::MAX_SORT_LINES (2^26) lines; the source has no limit
The comparator report is buffered up to MAX_LOG_BYTES (256 MiB) and a cut report is announced on stderr; the verdict is unaffected
-sort compares in memory; no temporary files are written
Integer parameters beyond i32 never reach the tool (the framework's readers refuse them); the tool's own conversion is defensive
